style.name: Gothic archival science fantasy
style.scope: primary for key art, hidden colonization systems, symbolic images, and explicitly advanced environments; ordinary surface-civilization packets take precedence
locked_traits: antique gold light used for evidence, truth, integration, and constructive power
deep crimson and ember red used for coercion, corruption, false authority, and fracture
living green used for growth, repair, adaptation, cultivation, and ecological intelligence
clear blue used for communication, coordination, shared infrastructure, and interplanetary connection
monumental gothic architecture fused with restrained future technology
fine sacred geometry, orbital diagrams, branching circuitry, crowns, archives, and throne motifs
painterly photorealism with tactile skin, cloth, metal, smoke, dust, and luminous linework
high contrast chiaroscuro with controlled rim light
solemn cinematic scale without generic superhero posing
composition_rules: Use darkness as negative space rather than filling every area with detail.
Keep red and gold narratively separated until a scene deliberately brings them into conflict.
Use green for living development and repair, not as a generic positive glow.
Use blue for connection and coordinated systems, not as generic cyberpunk atmosphere.
Use geometry as an information or reality system, not as decoration alone.
Reserve clean space for typography on poster and website compositions.
Generate artwork without text whenever exact copy matters.
avoid: flat vector illustration unless explicitly requested
logos, watermarks, signatures, and real-world insignia
imitation of a named living artist

documented_limitations: recurring-character and brand consistency can drift across generations
precise placement can fail in structured or layout-sensitive compositions
precise text placement and clarity can fail
complex prompts can have substantial latency

render_style_instructions.painterly-photorealism: tactile painterly photorealism with natural anatomy, material texture, and restrained cinematic finish
render_style_instructions.cinematic-photorealism: credible cinematic photography with natural skin, practical light, real materials, and no painterly or plastic rendering
render_style_instructions.archival-documentary: period-plausible documentary photography with era-appropriate optics, exposure, grain, materials, and staging

composition_modes.KEY-ART: Iconic promotional composition with deliberate negative space.
composition_modes.NARRATIVE-CINEMA: Scene-driven blocking with a readable dramatic instant; default for story scenes.
composition_modes.OBSERVATIONAL: Observed life; subjects may be small, occluded, off-center, or subordinate to place.
composition_modes.ORDINARY-LIFE: Mundane activity and social context; avoid heroic posing and visual privilege.

compiler.surface_hidden_rule: The resolved era and surface layer control visible civilization. Advanced colonization infrastructure remains hidden, mediated, disguised, or restricted unless the scene explicitly authorizes visibility.
compiler.ordinary_surface_style_rule: For ordinary surface scenes with no advanced-colony visibility, use natural era/location light, materials, architecture, and clothing. Project colors may appear only through motivated story evidence or cognition energy. Do not impose near-black key-art lighting, monumental gothic architecture, sacred geometry, or futuristic styling.

1940s.visible_life: wartime scarcity and industrial mobilization; practical structured clothing, durable natural fabrics, repair and reuse, with ordinary homes, shops, offices, schools, farms, transit, and civic life still present
1940s.technology_media: radio, print, newsreels, wired telephones, mail, typewriters, switchboards, analog instruments, paper files, vacuum-tube and electromechanical systems
1940s.transport_infrastructure: mechanically simple cars, rail, buses, walking, bicycles, shipping, propeller aviation, factories, warehouses, shipyards, workshops, brick, steel, wood, plaster, and incandescent light
1940s.guardrails: no smartphones, flat screens, LEDs, digital interfaces, modern tactical gear, contemporary casualwear, holograms, or visible colonization technology without explicit cause

1950s.visible_life: comparatively formal dress with growing casual sportswear; expanding household consumption, appliances, mass retail, automobile ownership, television, and residential development across varied urban, rural, and working-class settings
1950s.technology_media: television joins radio, print, landline phones, and physical mail; electrical appliances and purpose-built consumer equipment become increasingly visible
1950s.transport_infrastructure: cars, buses, rail, road networks, parking, and expanding commercial aviation; cleaner postwar modernism coexists with older urban and industrial fabric
1950s.guardrails: do not reduce the decade to an idealized suburb or erase apartments, transit, factories, hospitals, schools, offices, farms, and civic buildings

1960s.visible_life: tailored earlier-decade clothing coexists with increasingly casual, colorful, geometric, synthetic, youth-driven, and later bohemian styles
1960s.technology_media: widespread television, radio, records, print, landlines, paper-heavy offices, typewriters, mechanical calculators, duplicating equipment, and specialized centralized computers
1960s.transport_infrastructure: car-oriented development, buses, rail, commercial jets, modernist civic complexes, campuses, towers, and older neighborhoods
1960s.guardrails: space-age design is a cultural influence, not evidence of accessible colonization hardware

1970s.visible_life: eclectic fashion including denim, synthetics, wider trousers, workwear, sportswear, bohemian clothing, bold patterns, and increasingly informal homes and offices
1970s.technology_media: television, FM radio, records and tapes, telephones, print, calculators, electronic instruments, early digital systems, centralized computing, and rare late-decade personal computers
1970s.transport_infrastructure: mature car, transit, rail, and aviation systems; warm woods, plastics, earth tones, patterned textiles, modular furnishings, and analog bureaucratic institutions
1970s.guardrails: no ubiquitous PCs, internet culture, flat displays, smartphones, or modern surveillance interfaces

1980s.visible_life: assertive silhouettes, strong shoulders, bold colors, sportswear, business power dressing, street styles, and visible subcultural variation
1980s.technology_media: bulky personal computers, CRTs, floppy disks, wired keyboards, printers, fax machines, landlines, typewriters, cassette and video media, with paper processes still dominant
1980s.transport_infrastructure: car-dominant urban and suburban commerce, routine aviation, analog bureaucracy, and islands of desk-bound digital equipment
1980s.guardrails: computers remain bulky, wired, and visibly separate from the environment; no always-connected contemporary behavior

1990s.visible_life: broad casualization, jeans, loose or oversized layers, simple silhouettes, sneakers, and subculture-driven clothing
1990s.technology_media: ordinary desktop computers and growing laptops, CRTs, floppy disks, CDs, pagers, early mobile phones, fax, landlines, camcorders, dial-up, email, and an emerging public web
1990s.transport_infrastructure: mature cars and aviation, printed maps and signs, recognizable late-century architecture with digital change occurring inside otherwise ordinary spaces
1990s.guardrails: no modern smartphones, ubiquitous wireless connectivity, current flat-panel ecosystems, social-media behavior, or contemporary minimalist technology interiors

2000s.visible_life: casual media-driven clothing, denim, layered outfits, cargo and sportswear, fitted and loose silhouettes, and increasingly rapid trend turnover
2000s.technology_media: common desktops and laptops, broadband growth, widespread mobile phones, email, websites, digital photography, portable music, messaging, early social platforms, CDs and DVDs, with smartphones appearing only late
2000s.transport_infrastructure: increasingly networked offices and public spaces, transitional CRT-to-flat-panel displays, fixed workstations, cars, transit, and routine aviation
2000s.guardrails: resolve early, middle, or late decade when important; do not make a 2001-equivalent scene look like 2009

2010s.visible_life: smartphone-centered behavior, highly informal globally networked fashion, athleisure, sneakers, streetwear, slim tailoring, revival cycles, and persistent regional variation
2010s.technology_media: mobile internet, apps, social platforms, streaming, cloud services, GPS, digital photography, laptops, tablets, and flat-panel displays
2010s.transport_infrastructure: heavily networked offices, schools, retail, and services; app-mediated transport, delivery, navigation, and commerce in otherwise recognizable built environments
2010s.guardrails: do not make every contemporary space a minimalist technology-company interior; older buildings, vehicles, homes, and analog remnants remain common

2020s.visible_life: recognizable contemporary surface life with eclectic revival-driven casualwear, athleisure, streetwear, workwear, technical fabrics, sneakers, and both oversized and fitted silhouettes
2020s.technology_media: smartphones, broadband, streaming, cloud services, digital payments, delivery platforms, video calls, wireless earbuds, laptops, connected services, and frequent online coordination
2020s.transport_infrastructure: familiar contemporary vehicles, transit, aviation, retail, schools, hospitals, offices, apartments, suburbs, civic buildings, and public spaces with embedded screen-based digital systems
2020s.guardrails: Luminai, synthetics, and hidden colony AI do not justify cyberpunk streets, holograms, or futuristic consumer devices; advanced infrastructure appears only when the scene crosses that boundary

scene_workspace.policy: Feedback is scene-local by default. No candidate image, review, or repeated preference changes character authority, world definitions, or canon without an explicit promotion record.

luminai.behavior: coherent energy integrated with the person's body, attention, and breathing; strongest around cognition and embodied identity
luminai.palette: use antique/luminous gold for integration and truth, with clear blue only when communication or coordination is active

controls.coherence: coherent and continuous with breathing, attention, and movement; never random lightning or a separate figure

luminai.observer_rule: This is the default visual-production representation; whether and how in-world observers perceive it remains unresolved.

daemon.form: energy radiating from the integrated human, never a separate person, monster, or humanoid companion
daemon.behavior: the same embodied energy pattern made constricted, recursive, fractured, or misaligned by corrupted feedback and manufactured reality
daemon.palette: use deep crimson and ember red for coercion, corruption, and fracture without turning the field into fire or supernatural possession

rejuvenation_system.visual_rule: show outcomes through healthy tissue, movement, recovery, and apparent age; do not invent a glowing chamber, beam, or single miracle device unless a treatment scene requires definition

visual_entity_graph.policy: Graph nodes point to existing registry payloads and vault sources. They do not duplicate or establish story facts.
